props.title: The Little Drummer Boy Book II
props.initialSlug: A young drummer seeks to save a silver bell for Jesus

sections.content: The 1976 Rankin/Bass animated sequel **The Little Drummer Boy Book II** continues the studio's signature stop-motion "Animagic" style established in classics like **Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer** (1964). Following the success of **The Little Drummer Boy** (1968), this sequel expands on Aaron's story while incorporating the traditional Christmas themes Rankin/Bass excelled at. Like their other holiday specials **Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town** (1970) and **The Year Without a Santa Claus** (1974), it features memorable musical numbers and character designs by Paul Coker Jr.

sections.content: The sequel's plot involving silver bells and a fire in the temple allows Rankin/Bass to explore deeper themes of faith, sacrifice and redemption - hallmarks of their best work like **The First Christmas: The Story of the First Christmas Snow** (1975) and **Nestor, the Long-Eared Christmas Donkey** (1977). The voice talent includes Zero Mostel as Brutus and Greer Garson as the narrator, bringing gravitas to the production similar to Fred Astaire's narration in **Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town** (1970).

While less known than the original, Book II demonstrates Rankin/Bass's commitment to quality holiday programming in the mid-1970s, a period that also produced **'Twas the Night Before Christmas** (1974) and **Frosty's Winter Wonderland** (1976). The studio's distinctive animation style and earnest storytelling approach influenced later holiday specials like **The First Christmas** (1975) and **Pinocchio's Christmas** (1980). sections.content: The Little Drummer Boy series represents Rankin/Bass's approach to religious Christmas stories, which they balanced with secular tales throughout the 1970s. Their careful handling of faith-based material, also seen in **The First Easter Rabbit** (1976) and **The Stingiest Man in Town** (1978), helped establish them as trusted creators of family holiday entertainment.
